en: Buddhavamsa 23.
The Lineage of Buddha Vessabhū:
“In that very same aeon of adornment (maṇḍakappa),”
Unequaled and without rival,
the Leader named Vessabhū appeared in the world.
Truly, the fire of passion was ablaze,
yet at that time he conquered the realm of cravings;
like an elephant breaking its bonds, he severed them.
He attained supreme enlightenment while Vessabhū,
the Leader of the World, was setting in motion the Wheel of Dhamma.
There was the first realization for eighty thousand crores.
And when he had departed on his journey through the country...
In the Elder of the World, the Bull among Men,
there occurred a second realization for seventy thousand times ten million beings.
Dispelling their great delusion,
he performs a miracle;
humans and gods have gathered together.
In the ten-thousandfold world system together with its devas,
having seen a great marvel,
a wonder that makes the hair stand on end;
Sixty million devas and humans attained awakening;
there were three such assemblies.
Of Vessabhu, the great seer;
of those whose taints are exhausted, who are stainless,
whose minds are peaceful, and who are steadfast.
The first assembly consisted of eighty thousand bhikkhus;
the second assembly consisted of seventy thousand bhikkhus.
The second assembly took place;
the third assembly consisted of sixty thousand bhikkhus.
I was, at that time, the legitimate son of the Great Seer, who was terrified by the fear of old age and other such ills.
The kshatriya named Sudassana,
having invited the Great Hero and given a most costly gift;
With food, drink, and clothing,
I made offerings to the Victor together with his Saṅgha;
to that peerless Buddha, I paid homage.
Having heard the sublime Dhamma, I delighted in going forth after the supreme Wheel had been set in motion.
Having performed a great act of giving,
untiring day and night,
he attained the going-forth endowed with excellence.
I went forth in the presence of the Victor.
Endowed with conduct and virtue, established in observance, moral discipline, and concentration;
Seeking omniscience,
I take delight in the Conqueror’s teaching;
having attained the joy of faith, I rejoice.
I pay homage to the Buddha,
the Teacher; joy arises within me for the very sake of enlightenment.
Knowing that his mind was not turning back,
the Sambuddha said this:
“In the thirty-first aeon from now...”
"This one shall become a Buddha.
There was a delightful city called Kapila... [and so forth].
“...we shall be present before him.
Having heard his words,
my mind became even more serene.
I resolved upon a further vow for the fulfillment of the ten perfections.
[There was] a city named Anoma.
The Kṣatriya father was named Suppatīta,
and the mother of Vessabhu, the Great Seer, was named Yasavatī.
For six thousand years he dwelt in the household life;
[he was] Ruci, Suruci, and Rativaḍḍhana.
There were three supreme palaces,
and thirty thousand women adorned with ornaments.
That woman was named Sucittā,
and his son was named Suppabuddha.
Having seen four omens, [he departed].
He went forth from his palanquin;
for six months, the Supreme Person practiced the course of striving.
Being entreated by Brahmā,
the World-Leader Vessabhū,
the Great Hero, set the Wheel of Dhamma in motion.
In Aruṇārāma, the Supreme among Men had Soṇa and Uttara as his two chief disciples.
Upasanta was the attendant of the great seer Vessabhu;
and Rāmā and Samālā as well.
were his chief female disciples;
the Bodhi tree of that Blessed One is called Mahāsāla.
Sotthika and Rambha were the foremost attendants;
so too were Gotamī and Sirimā.
They were his foremost attendants.
Sixty ratanas in height, resembling a sacrificial pillar made of gold;
A ray of light issues from his body,
like a fire on a mountain at night.
For sixty thousand years,
Such was the lifespan of that Great Sage;
remaining for that long,
he delivered many people across.
Having made the Dhamma widespread and having analyzed it for the great multitude,
and having established the ship of the Dhamma—
He has attained Nibbāna along with his disciples—
worthy of being seen by all people,
both in his dwelling and in his modes of conduct.
All that has vanished;
are not all conditioned things empty?
Vessabhū, the supreme Victor, the Teacher—
He attained final Nibbāna in the Khemārāma monastery;
his relics were widely distributed throughout various regions.
The lineage of the Blessed One Vessabhu is the twenty-first.
